issues.claim: audit_md, 'What it means for customers': '...reaches a blank ad page or another chain's booking screen, not this salon.' Also severity_reason: 'the other into a different chain's booking flow' and the outreach email: 'hairbarnyc.com opens a different chain's booking screen'.
issues.problem: Stated as fact, but it is not supported and is probably wrong. The auditor's own founder_md lists the same point as an open question ('Is the North Brunswick salon still part of the Hair Bar NYC chain, or independent with an old chain link left on the profile?'), so the two documents contradict each other. Evidence points the other way: this is the salon's own first website field on its Google profile, Google returns this profile first for a search of 'Hair Bar NYC North Brunswick NJ' and shows no separate Hair Bar listing in New Jersey, the Giftly listing for the same address carries a review tip mentioning '24 K Hairbar keratin treatment', and directory listings name the business 'Hair Bar NYC @ Salon G' at 1727 US-130 (callupcontact.com, localstylist.com). None of that proves a franchise relationship, but it means 'a different chain, not this salon' cannot be printed or said to the owner.
issues.fix: Replace the assertion with what was actually observed and sourced: 'The link goes to Hair Bar NYC's public booking site, whose location list shows nine salons in New York and Florida and no New Jersey location, so a customer who follows it cannot book at this address.' Delete 'another chain's' / 'a different chain's' from audit_md, severity_reason and both outreach scripts, and keep the affiliation question in founder_md's open questions.

issues.claim: The lead is treated throughout as an independent salon (role requires 'not a chain or franchise'), and fix step 3 is 'Remove hairbarnyc.com too unless the salon is still part of that chain.'
issues.problem: The business may be a Hair Bar NYC franchise location ('Hair Bar NYC @ Salon G'). I could not confirm or rule this out from a primary source: hairbarnyc.com/locations/ is a corporate page showing nine NY/FL salons, the booking site shows the same nine, and third-party pages that use the 'Hair Bar NYC @ Salon G' name are aggregator/directory sites I could not open for verification (Cloudflare check on localstylist.com, timeout on salonlookup.com). If it is a franchise, the website links on the profile may be controlled by the franchisor, so telling the owner to remove them would be bad advice.
issues.fix: Before any outreach, have someone confirm the relationship (look at the salon's own signage/materials, or the owner's answer on a first call) and record it. If it is a Hair Bar NYC franchise, either drop the lead as a chain/franchise or limit the audit to the dead domain, which is the salon's own.
